svg.title: Continuous State (Kalman) vs Discrete State (HMM)
svg.desc: Both share the same hidden Markov skeleton; whether the state space is a real vector or a finite set of regimes turns the recursion into an integral or a sum.
svg.text: A state flowing through real vectors vs one moving among a few regimes
Transition matrix T and shock variance Q
Eigenvalues of T — the decay rate
A finite set of K regimes
The state flows through real values
The observation level moves with the state
The state moves among a few regimes
When the regime switches, the observations change
The output is a mean and a variance
The value and its uncertainty come out together
The output is a posterior per regime
Crossing 0.5 is the line that calls the regime
Both share the same skeleton: hidden state → observation.
A continuous state gives an integral and a variance; a discrete state gives a sum and a probability.
only how the past state is marginalized out
splits into an integral or a sum
